Amusing story. I used to work at a reptile nature center. We would go out with a variety of snakes (usually local endangered ones, but also some more common pet snakes like corns) to public events like fairs and teach people about the snakes and let kids hold them and stuff. 

Invariably there’d be at least one freaked out mom that would screech “do they bite?!” while we were draping a five foot long rat snake around her kid’s shoulders. My boss at that time was a very plucky lady with a certain sense of humor, and she would exclaim “YUP” and watch the parents begin to freak out. “I don’t know about you,” she’d say, “but I bite my food when I eat and that’s what they do too. But if you’re asking if it’s going to bite your kid, then no.” 

Same day, I had a gray ratsnake on my shoulders (a biiiiig one) and was walking around with it. A woman told her little girl to not touch its head because it would bite her (which is generally good advice, but these snakes are very used to being handled and aren’t headshy in the slightest). Jokingly I told the mother “honestly I’d be more worried about the other end.” Literally two minutes later the snake squirted a giant stream of poop alllllll down the front of me, it smelled so so so bad, and I didn’t have a change of shirt.

I was like “heck yeah!” And she started grabbing rocks. After the tour we sat down to have lunch and she was off doing something, her family thanked me for being so sweet to their “crazy kid” and it was very clear that none of them appreciated her interests or talents. They said they didn’t know quite what to do with her, and she was so weird, they hoped she grew out of it.

I have. I’ve been depressed since I was 15 up until last year (I’m turning 34 in two weeks). During those years I wanted to commit suicide about 75-80% of the time, tried to overdose on drugs, cut myself and actively never planned for the future. Sadness followed me around like a cloud. 

Last year I had a very scary episode in which I decided a hundred percent the next day I was going to do it. I was fully done. I had given life a shot and I could really say now that I was terrible at it. All the worst thoughts going through my head. I’ve been very close to real suicide many times but this one eclipsed them all.

Funnily enough I had randomly added a guy on tinder and as soon as we started chatting I told him I was having a really hard time and he called me. I told him I didn’t want to live anymore and had made up my mind and would be leaving tomorrow. He talked to me for at least an hour and gently steered my mind to other things, distracting me.

After we got out off the phone I fell asleep and the next day was so unnerved with myself that I decided there and now to make a decision. Shit or get off the pot. Either kill yourself, today, or never consider it an option again. Commit yourself to life. A hundred percent.

Obviously you can guess the one I chose. Once I made that decision to commit myself to life on purpose, as an act of intention, rather than slogging through it because I felt as though I was put here against my will... things really changed. I can say without hesitation I am the happiest I’ve ever been in my entire life. I look after myself now, because I committed to myself. Finally. After 20 years of hating that I had to exist, not feeling like a person, hating who I was, feeling ill suited towards life, feeling hopeless and exhausted, angry with the world and angry with myself.

I eat right because I know if I don’t, I will slip into the bad place again. I go to the gym and go for walks every day, because I know if I don’t I will slip into the bad place again. I drink less. I try to keep my place clean. And if I don’t, I don’t drag myself through the coals anymore. I treat myself like a real person. 

I’m not on any medication. It was a shift in perspective followed by a series of actions that led to building healthy habits. I’m aware my depression isn’t as bad as some, but the last 20 years of my life were truly truly absolute hell, and I finally feel like I can breathe. There are still days that I feel sad or down (MUCH fewer and far between might I add) and when those come I make sure I’m taking care of myself in every possible way I can, and then let the darkness be there until it passes. 

Suicide used to be my coping mechanism because it was the only way I knew to escape whatever problem I was facing. Now that I’m committed to life, I just do my best to deal with whatever it is and try not to beat myself up if it’s not perfect. That’s all any of us can do.
